title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: GAR 2 / PLAC — integritas; condition vs promised
pass_a_gloss: GAR. 2. Adam persevering in integrity was to be endowed with continuation and increase of goods both corporal and spiritual: Therefore also falling away from that integrity, it was fitting that he should be subject to evils both corporal and spiritual: why then would God not have wished those things signified by the name of death? PLAC. But perseverance in integrity and continuation of integrity are the same. But original integrity and original righteousness—how do they differ? He was therefore to be endowed with continuation, not of original righteousness (for this continuation was required as condition) but of all other goods. Further, integrity is opposed immediately to corruption: to fall away from integrity is to be corrupted; to lose integrity is to acquire corruption. The Learned Man therefore confounds the condition of the promise with the thing promised: nor is the antecedent of his argument true, unless it be understood of physical goods, or goods diverse from integrity itself or righteousness.
pass_b_english: GAR. 2. Adam, if he had persevered in integrity, was to be given continuance and increase of bodily and spiritual goods. Therefore, falling from that integrity, it was fitting he should lie under bodily and spiritual evils: why then should God not have meant those by the name of death?

PLAC. But perseverance in integrity and continuance of integrity are the same thing. And how do original integrity and original righteousness differ? So he was to be given continuance—not of original righteousness (for that continuance was required as the condition), but of all other goods. Integrity is opposed immediately to corruption: to fall from integrity is to be corrupted; to lose integrity is to gain corruption. So the learned man confounds the condition of the promise with the thing promised; and his antecedent is true only of physical goods, or goods other than integrity or righteousness itself.
source_text: GAR. 2. Adamus in integritate perseverans, bonorum & corporalium, & spiritualium continuatione & augmento donandus erat: Ergo & ab ea integritate deficiens, ut malis subiaceret, & corporalibus, & spiritualibus, consentaneum erat: quidni ergo Deus ea significata voluerit mortis nomine? PLAC. Atqui perseverantia in integritate & continuatio integritatis idem sunt. Integritas autem originalis & justitia originalis quid differunt? Erat igitur donandus continuatione, non justitiae originalis (haec enim continuatio exigebatur ut conditio) sed aliorum omnium bonorum. Porro integritas opponitur corruptioni immediate: deficere ab integritate est corrumpi, amittere integritatem est acquirere corruptionem. Confundit ergo Vir doctus conditionem promissionis cum re promissa: nec verum est argumenti ejus antecedens, nisi de bonis intelligatur physicis, seu ab ipsa integritate seu justitia diversis.
